topic.name: MET
topic.short_description: Receptor tyrosine kinase target in lung cancer
topic.seo_title: MET Biomarker in Lung Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore MET receptor tyrosine kinase as a lung cancer biomarker. Discover latest diagnostic advances, targeted therapies, and peer-reviewed research findings.
topic.seo_intro:
MET is a receptor tyrosine kinase that plays a significant role in cell growth and survival, making it an important focus in cancer research, particularly for lung cancer patients. When MET becomes abnormally activated through mutations, amplifications, or overexpression, it can drive cancer cell proliferation and contribute to treatment resistance. Understanding MET as a biomarker has become crucial for oncologists and researchers developing more precise diagnostic approaches and targeted treatment strategies.

Researchers have identified MET alterations in a subset of lung cancer patients, which has opened new avenues for personalized medicine. By detecting MET changes through advanced diagnostic techniques, physicians can better stratify patients and select those who may benefit from MET-targeted therapies. This biomarker-driven approach represents a shift toward precision oncology, where treatments are matched to each patient's unique tumor characteristics. Current studies are exploring how MET testing can improve treatment selection, predict response to therapy, and help overcome resistance to other targeted drugs.

On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed research articles examining MET as a biomarker in lung cancer diagnostics and treatment. These studies represent the current state of scientific investigation into how MET analysis can enhance patient outcomes and advance our understanding of cancer biology.

articles.title: Phase I Study of Telisotuzumab Adizutecan (Temab-A, ABBV-400), a Novel c-Met Antibody-Drug Conjugate, in Patients With Late-Line Colorectal Cancer and Advanced Solid Tumors.
articles.hook: Telisotuzumab adizutecan shows activity in advanced colorectal cancer patients
articles.summary: Early-stage testing shows Temab-A, a new drug targeting c-Met, has potential activity in advanced colorectal cancer and solid tumors.

articles.title: Risk of peripheral edema in cancer patients receiving MET inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.hook: MET inhibitors significantly increase peripheral edema risk in lung cancer patients
articles.summary: MET inhibitors used to treat cancer significantly increase the risk of peripheral edema, especially monoclonal antibodies and combination therapies.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of tepotinib vs capmatinib as subsequent therapy in MET exon 14-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer.
articles.summary: Tepotinib proves more cost-effective than capmatinib for treating advanced lung cancer with specific MET mutations in China.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Acquired Resistance Following Dual EGFR/MET Inhibition in MET-Amplified EGFR TKI-Resistant Lung Cancer.
articles.summary: Lung cancer patients resistant to dual EGFR/MET inhibitors develop various new mutations, some treatable with additional targeted drugs or amivantamab antibody therapy.

articles.title: Liquid biopsy-based detection of acquired MET resistance enables sequential targeted therapy in MET fusion-positive NSCLC.
articles.hook: Liquid biopsy detects MET resistance mutations...
articles.summary: Liquid biopsy blood tests detected drug-resistance mutations in lung cancer patients, enabling successful switch to alternative MET inhibitor therapy.

articles.title: Association of MUC3A P258S mutation with advanced phase CML structural and in silico insights.
articles.hook: MUC3A P258S mutation predicts Capmatinib response in advanced CML
articles.summary: A novel MUC3A mutation found exclusively in advanced chronic myeloid leukemia may serve as a progression biomarker and improve treatment response to Capmatinib.

articles.title: An Open-Label Phase I/II Study to Evaluate the Safety and prelimiBasnary Efficacy of Amivantamab and Tepotinib Combination in MET-altered Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
articles.summary: Researchers are testing whether combining two drugs, amivantamab and tepotinib, safely treats lung cancer with specific genetic mutations.

articles.title: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Telisotuzumab Adizutecan for the Treatment of Subjects With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors That Harbor MET Amplification
articles.summary: A new drug called telisotuzumab adizutecan is being tested to treat advanced solid tumors with MET amplification mutations.

articles.title: HRA00129-C004, a Novel c-Met Antibody-Drug Conjugate, Exerts Encouraging Antitumor Activities and Favorable Safety Profiles.
articles.summary: HRA00129-C004, a new cancer drug targeting c-Met protein, shows strong tumor-killing effects with good safety in early testing.

articles.title: Prognostic significance of metabolic parameters from l-methyl-11C-methionine PET/computed tomography before postoperative adjuvant therapy in patients with glioma.
articles.summary: A PET scan measuring methionine uptake before treatment predicts survival outcomes in glioma patients.
